title: Banned again for Generative AI
author: Roguelike-Engine103
selftext:
Hello community friends ... how do you deal with AI bigotry and its repercussions in your projects and hobby interests?

https://preview.redd.it/nztghq06iefg1.png?width=511&format=png&auto=webp&s=59f4e553fa4afc73da9a982e1f588d83a38ec4c5

The mod of the above sub heard the history of our game, r/21stCenturyHack  and how it uses Generative AI to remaster and maintain a classic DOS 1985 Terminal game, the first Roguelike, Hack 1.0.3 ... they have started banning me and my brother u/21stCenturyHack wherever we go on Reddit around Roguelikes.

comments.author: MysteriousPepper8908
comments.body: Unfortunately, niches like that can be heavily targeted by one mod on a power trip. The only real solution is to avoid disclosure as long as possible but it seems like the ship has sailed in that regard.

replies.author: Roguelike-Engine103
replies.body: Thank you for the interesting perspective. Am I understanding you correctly that you are suggesting we should conceal or hide the fact the project was made with help of Generative AI? It was of course also requiring hundreds of hour of labor of love too.

replies.author: MysteriousPepper8908
replies.body:
Unfortunately, yeah. A lot of people have binary thinking and don't understand that AI goes well beyond basic text prompting. It's like how 20 years ago people thought digital art was telling the computer what to make but now we have the added element of antis who will track you down on multiple platforms to harass you and Reddit mods that can unilaterally ban you from multiple subs they mod for because of their personal vendetta. 


Until the irrational level of hate dies down, disclosing AI use is just too hazardous. You need to once you're on Steam or risk getting delisted but don't do it prematurely.

replies.author: Microtom_
replies.body:
Bro, there's nothing wrong with AI. These people use games engines. Game engines were made to make developing games easier. They are a level of abstraction that permits us to not have to program games in a straight programming language.

And programming languages were made to prevent us from having to write machine code or assembly. 

We make games not to make games. We make games to have games to play. The shortest path is always the right one. 👍

replies.author: Other-Football72
replies.body:
This is what it all boils down to: technology and tools come and go, and are used to make some task quicker, easier, or more efficient. 

The people most butthurt are the ones whose skills revolve around doing things that machines are now doing in 1/1,000,000th the time with every-increasing quality. They moan and whine about a lack of soul, or suddenly using electricity is the end of the world, but they're mostly just afraid and desperate.

comments.author: Cool-Chemical-5629
comments.body:
I'm confused. What did the mod mean by "after learning more about its history"? What's its history? Did you steal or kill someone to make the game or something like that? Or is it really just that they generally dislike that you used AI in the process?

Do they even realize how much the AI is nowadays involved in the game development in general? Even if you made the assets manually in Photoshop, chances are you'd be using one, or multiple AI powered tools in the Photoshop itself, because guess what! Nowadays the Photoshop is filled with them to the brim and relies on them HEAVILY!

To me this seems like straight up bullying and witch hunt which is ridiculous, especially if the mod is a dev himself. How would they like it if someone else was this much prejudiced against them and ban them on multiple different communities, just because they don't like X or Y thing about their own game?

If you don't like someone's opinions, ideas or creations, block them on your personal account, but DON'T ABUSE your power as a moderator in order to block them from an entire community! This is backwards and insane level of censorship! In 21st century, for Christ's sake.

replies.author: MissItalia2022
replies.body: Asking a moderator not to abuse their authority is like asking a 13 year old boy to stop beating their dick.

replies.author: Roguelike-Engine103
replies.body: Initially we posted about this game on Nethack and other Roguelike subs because we thought the community would embrace the idea of preserving this memory from 1985 and modernizing it for the next generation of Hackers. We were met with hate and accusations of "AI slop" and using "AI that steals from the work of uncredited artists" and "why didn't we commission an artist?", stuff like that. I said that we didn't have the money for an artist and the in-game credits clearly state we used Adobe Firefly generative AI, which also grants us indemnification for the generated results. So we weren't trying to hide anything. Anyway we got banned from there and a few other Roguelike subs because of the AI fighting.

replies.author: Cool-Chemical-5629
replies.body: And letting the haters win? Nah, don't give up. Looks like you're pretty far in the progress. Keep going. Like I mentioned, Valve acknowledges and allows it, so as long as you stay within the lines of their rules, you should be pretty much fine. Your game wouldn't be the first one created that way and certainly not the last one there ever will be. The AI haters are the ones who are fighting the war which is already lost here, because the AI is already such a significant part of our daily lives (not just LLMs but in many other ways too) it's basically already here to stay and not going anywhere. AI haters will eventually have to give up hating on AI and move on.

replies.author: gefahr
replies.body:
Whether they like it or not, AI-assisted development (in many forms) is a big part of the future of game dev. I'm not even talking about the current state of things, but imagine where they'll be in 2-3 years.

Don't give up, these people will obsolete themselves.

After 3 years I've got a discord server for my passion-project-turned-job with nearly 5k members and they are some of the nicest and most helpful people I've met.

replies.author: Douglas12dsd
replies.body:
> Disclosure means that they will bully and abuse you regardless of the amount of time and energy that you've spent.


I've heard of a case where a dev sent a key for their game to someone because they introduced themselves as good willing reviewer... Just to be the first one in 30 positive reviews to give a bad review just because it used AI.


I would love to disclose AI use not because of their brigade, but just to motivate our fellows AI devs... But unfortunately, as you said, is a "noob trap" of current game market.


And even fully disclosure can be hurtful, since saying you not used as much AI as you really used can save up some headaches.

So ai is likely not going to be welcome in any artistic niche since it takes all of the human soul out of the games

comments.author: Roenbaeck
comments.body: I've used AI extensively over the last couple of years to realize a number of my ever growing list of *someday* projects, and I have always been transparent about the use of AI. The backlashes from communities have many times been harsh, but honestly, the more I've accomplished the more I've realized that these are from luddites, hopelessly falling behind in this paradigm shift. Just disregard these people, get stuff done, and have fun. I know I am.

comments.author: imnotabot303
comments.body:
Unfortunately witch hunts for AI are quite prolific on most subs on Reddit, especially art and game dev subs.

Someone could use AI to help make a free tool and there will still be people attacking them for using it.

Being anti AI is just the latest easy way to make people feel morally superior and farm easy upvotes.

Saying you used AI in any sub that is not an AI related sub is basically just putting a target on yourself for online hate and witch hunts. Then people wonder why everyone isn't upfront about stating they use it. Most of them don't even care how it was used, they just hear AI and immediately put it into the AI slop category.

replies.author: Roguelike-Engine103
replies.body: The definition of bigotry is "[obstinate](https://www.google.com/search?sca_esv=b51a820206a0f7d2&sxsrf=ANbL-n6SsRgaH3fscKeKPLFIsED8eB-M9w:1769527703131&q=obstinate&si=AL3DRZENm3Vb5fKAKJGBSnAO98GG0N5r3sOVEHnRFxYT-Fj_AWZl-wuPPwzSFB26h5G_JOUYR_UYFZNonYdtrEExysr1V31aftlQp1XL0pRUIcyFSB3V_CE%3D&expnd=1&sa=X&sqi=2&ved=2ahUKEwiQhamxhKySAxUJiO4BHT32N3YQyecJegQIHhAQ) or [unreasonable](https://www.google.com/search?sca_esv=b51a820206a0f7d2&sxsrf=ANbL-n6SsRgaH3fscKeKPLFIsED8eB-M9w:1769527703131&q=unreasonable&si=AL3DRZEMXBqaLXSV-mI4aprR_vyyTWot9FpfPeUrxhTbhqzSR4a2DDicMwhHzM1d_WRRFkfZbDnst3KVRbYxAHHlslBZ4VdKx4CxwdZyimg9O707WLaM8IA%3D&expnd=1&sa=X&sqi=2&ved=2ahUKEwiQhamxhKySAxUJiO4BHT32N3YQyecJegQIHhAR) attachment to a belief, opinion, or [faction](https://www.google.com/search?sca_esv=b51a820206a0f7d2&sxsrf=ANbL-n6SsRgaH3fscKeKPLFIsED8eB-M9w:1769527703131&q=faction&si=AL3DRZFEkDaZmmb0xlmPYpZ16WK3GW9M7XyYg3rpLfmNAhkUzDy8v1m6L_wVhSyfvdBSTqtNX9bLrNcVWYWO_iswBhFbZ0UI41DCOiRL38V9TF2fr7OkL3I%3D&expnd=1&sa=X&sqi=2&ved=2ahUKEwiQhamxhKySAxUJiO4BHT32N3YQyecJegQIHhAS), in particular prejudice against a person or people on the basis of their membership of a particular group." In this case the mods and users of various subs have an unreasonable belief that any use of Generative AI is "BAD" and any gamedev using it is "BAD". Also when they ban you for no reason other than Generative AI, that is the purest definition of bigotry.
